newsitem.title: USA: Kevorkian brings 43rd assisted death to hospital.
newsitem.headline: Kevorkian brings 43rd assisted death to hospital.

text.p: Assisted suicide doctor Jack Kevorkian dropped off the body of a 55-year-old Illinois woman at a hospital emergency room on Thursday, hours after police detained him as he left a meeting with the woman.
Kevorkian brought the woman's body to William Beaumont Hospital in Royal Oak and identified her as Nancy DeSoto of Bourbonnais, Illinois, a hospital spokeswoman said.
It was the 43rd death Kevorkian has acknowledged attending since he began his doctor-assisted suicide crusade in 1990.

Kevorkian's lawyer, Geoffrey Fieger, said DeSoto was a florist who suffered from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, known as Lou Gehrig's disease, which left her paralysed and in a wheelchair. She died in suburban Detroit with Kevorkian, her husband, Joseph, and a friend present, Fieger said.

On Wednesday night, police stopped the suicide activist in the parking lot of the Dunes Motel in Royal Oak after he left a meeting with DeSoto and Janet Good, one of his associates, Fieger said. Police detained him for about an hour but did not arrest him.

DeSoto remained in her room at the motel after the meeting, and officers later ordered the motel's manager to open the door to her room, Fieger said. She ordered them out because they did not have a warrant.
Fieger also accused police of illegally tapping Kevorkian's telephone line, saying they knew about the meeting in advance.
But Royal Oak Police Commander Don Novak said officers routinely patrol the Dunes and several other nearby motels for prostitution and drug dealing.
"The officers recognised Kevorkian's car in the parking lot of a motel half a mile from Beaumont Hospital," Novak said. "They were concerned about someone's safety."
A similar incident occurred on Sept. 6 when police in nearby West Bloomfield Township broke up a meeting between Kevorkian and a patient in a hotel room.
The patient, 60-year-old Isabel Correa, of Fresno, California, died the next day with Kevorkian's help. She suffered from a spinal cord disorder that left her bound to a wheelchair.
